column1: # ---- 03-contracts/C2 ----
C2 carries the ValuationBundle payload at version 1.0 from L2 to L3 and is the load-bearing seam.
Everything the Planner knows about economics arrives through C2, expressed in the closed algebra of five shapes.
The Planner has no access to Belief, to prices, or to scenario arrays.
compositionOrder records the stages actually applied, in order, for audit.
effectCoverage records which view owned which effect this tick.
unclaimedEffects are priced at zero, and an empty unclaimedEffects is the expected case.
Terms refer to decision variables by a closed enumeration: the Planner owns the variables and Valuation may only name them.
The decision variable vocabulary is pCharge, pDischarge, soc, socTerminal, pPoi, zPeak, vDaBuy, vDaSell, vIdBuy, vIdSell, rUp, rDn, eAfrrUp, eAfrrDn, eImbalance, q and aDel.
pCharge and pDischarge are in the battery frame, pPoi and zPeak in the POI frame.
aDel spans the accumulators j in {(3),(5),(6),(9),(11),(26),(29)}.
Like zPeak, aDel is not a free decision because the Planner's state equations pin it, but a term must be able to name it because DelineationView prices it at λ_j = ∂V_del/∂A_j.
The C2 vocabulary is meter-shaped only: no symbol attributes energy to a path or to a named installation.
The delineation's per-slot variables Z1NB, Z1NE, Z2V, Z2E and the MIN selectors are Planner-internal and deliberately absent from C2, because no lever may carry a delineation coefficient.
Adding a symbol to the decision variable vocabulary is a major version bump.
Every term carries a common header of termId, originView, effect, base, slots, mandatory and confidence.
termId is stable and unique within the bundle.
The effect field is from the closed enumeration and is the basis of the exclusivity check.
The base field is one of PoiImport, BatteryThroughput, MarketVolume, TerminalSoc, ReserveCapacity or Delineation.
If mandatory is true, dropping the term invalidates the plan, and peak protection is mandatory.
The confidence field is propagated from input quality, feeds riskProfile, and never drives a branch.
A LinearTerm carries a variable from the vocabulary, a per-slot coefficient in EUR per variable unit, and a sense of Maximize or Minimize.
A PwlTerm carries the abscissa variable, strictly increasing breakpointsX in variable units, breakpointsY in EUR, a curvature, a sense, and an extrapolation of Clamp or Forbid.
A PwlTerm's curvature is verified against the breakpoints and not trusted.
An extrapolation of Forbid adds bounds at the end breakpoints.
The combinations (Concave, Maximize) and (Convex, Minimize) require no binaries and are LP-exact.
Any other curvature-sense combination, and any General curvature, requires SOS2 or binaries.
The bundle must declare the binary count in problemClassHint so a solve-time regression is attributable to a specific economic modelling choice.
An EpigraphTerm carries epigraphVar, dominates, overSlots, floor, unitPrice and prorationFactor.
The overSlots subset is how HLZF is expressed.
The epigraph floor is the realised peak so far, taken from L0.
prorationFactor is the fraction of the accounting period inside this horizon.
Because the horizon is shorter than the accounting period, the full period charge must not be applied to a partial window.
The remaining accounting-period value is carried by V.
Mis-setting prorationFactor is a classic overweighting of peak.

A BoundTerm carries a target variable or linear expression, per-slot lower and upper bounds either of which may be null for a one-sided bound, a reason, and an optional softPenalty where null means a hard bound.
A BoundTerm's reason is one of Physical, Contractual, Liquidity, Risk or Regulatory.
Feasibility restoration relaxes bounds in a declared order: Risk first, then Liquidity, and never Physical or Regulatory.
Without the reason tag an infeasible model can only be relaxed blindly.

A CouplingConstraint carries a kind from the closed set ReserveCorridor, ReservePowerHeadroom, Commitment, ChanceConstraint or Custom, its rows as linear rows per slot or per block, a scenarioScope, and a declared introducesBinaries count.
A CouplingConstraint's declared introducesBinaries is checked against what is built.
The value function is carried separately from the term list because it is structurally distinctive and its staleness is handled specially.
vSocBreakpointsX is strictly increasing and spans [socMin, socMax].
vSocSlopes is strictly decreasing, which is concavity, and this is asserted.
The value function is conditioned on (peakState, qualState, calendarContext).
The value function carries producedAt, the slot when the slow loop produced it, and a validityHorizon beyond which a staleness penalty applies.
stalenessPenalty is a shrink factor in [0,1] applied when the value function is stale.
The value function carries an artefactHash for the Merkle chain.
rUpMax and rDnMax are the per-block reserve envelope from prequalification and asset limits.
capacityValueCurveUp and capacityValueCurveDn are per-block PwlTerms, concave in offered MW, carrying the expected value of the bid curve.
deliveryObligation carries already-confirmed awards from L0 as a hard commitment.
deliveryObligation is separated from the offer decision because confirmed awards are physical obligations that survive every degradation mode, whereas offers are decisions.
The risk profile is how input quality reaches the optimisation without becoming control flow.
cvarLevel is widened when quality degrades.
cvarWeight is the weight on the CVaR term against expectation.
chanceLevel is the ε for SOC feasibility chance constraints.
positionScale is a multiplier in [0,1] on speculative position bounds.
peakSafetyMarginKw is added to the epigraph floor under degraded load quality.
driverSummary records which quality issues moved which parameter, for the audit trail.
The problem class hint is computed by the composer from the terms present, before the solver sees anything.
isLinearProgram is true when no term introduces a binary.
binariesByOrigin attributes the binary count to the term that caused it.
The problem class hint is the instrument that keeps solve time explainable, and when a solve slows down binariesByOrigin names the term responsible.
No (effect, variable, slot) triple is priced by more than one term, and violation is a HALT for double counting.
Every term's originView is the owner of its effect in the ownership matrix, and violation is a HALT.
Every term references only symbols in the C2 vocabulary, and violation is a HALT.
Every mandatory term is present, and violation is a HALT.
unclaimedEffects are logged, and if any is in the critical set the engine escalates.
No scenario array and no Belief handle appears anywhere in the bundle, and violation is a HALT.
compositionOrder satisfies the stage precondition table, and violation is a HALT.
binariesByOrigin sums to binaryCount, and violation warns.
Every BoundTerm has a reason and no Physical bound is soft, and violation is a HALT.
FillProbView emits only BoundTerms and has no priced term, and violation is a HALT.
No term references a provenance flow attributing energy to a path or to a named installation, and violation is a HALT.
Prices do not cross C2: the Planner sees coefficients on variables rather than a price series, which is what stops it re-deriving economics.
Scenario arrays do not cross C2, and scenario structure reaches the Planner only through CouplingConstraint rows with a scenarioScope and through terms already aggregated by Valuation.
Delegates and expression trees do not cross C2.
Nothing from Belief crosses C2 unpriced: if the Planner needs it, a view must own it and price or bound it.
